1	"""CJK Bigram Confusion Disambiguation Memory.
2	
3	The base confusion_disambiguation_memory system uses a tokenizer that matches
4	only ASCII characters ([A-Za-z0-9]+).  For Chinese-language legal text this
5	produces near-zero overlap on every pair of examples — similarity is driven
6	solely by shared date/number strings, making retrieval essentially random and
7	making the confusion matrix signal useless (because every retrieved example
8	looks equally similar regardless of content).
9	
10	This system replaces the tokenizer with CJK character bigrams plus ASCII
11	tokens.  Bigrams over Chinese characters give genuine semantic overlap that
12	tracks shared legal concepts and factual context, restoring the intended
13	behaviour of the confusion disambiguation retrieval algorithm.
14	
15	Everything else — the confusion matrix, the disambiguation injection logic,
16	the prompt template, the serialisation — is identical to the base system.
17	The hypothesis is therefore tightly controlled: if accuracy improves, it is
18	because real similarity signal was absent and bigrams supply it.
19	"""
